title: Fraud by wire, radio, or television (for comparison)
instrument: 18 U.S.C. 1343, with the elements as summarised in the DOJ Criminal Resource Manual 941 (archived)
binding_note: A criminal statute, and courts decide whether it applies. The circuits state the elements in different words; the DOJ page lists several formulations.

in_force.note: United States Code, 2024 edition, as published on govinfo.

sources.publisher: US Government Publishing Office, govinfo (United States Code, 2024 edition)
US Department of Justice (archived Criminal Resource Manual)
sources.note: Scripted fetches got a changing 2.7 KB challenge page, so the hash is SHA-256 over the UTF-8 text of the rendered <main> element (2,585 bytes). The page is marked archived and may be outdated.

quotes.text: Whoever, having devised or intending to devise any scheme or artifice to defraud, or for obtaining money or property by means of false or fraudulent pretenses, representations, or promises, transmits or causes to be transmitted by means of wire, radio, or television communication in interstate or foreign commerce, any writings, signs, signals, pictures, or sounds for the purpose of executing such scheme or artifice,

quotes.locator: CRM 941, quoting United States v. Maxwell, 920 F.2d 1028, 1035 (D.C. Cir. 1990)
quotes.text: Wire fraud requires proof of (1) a scheme to defraud; and (2) the use of an interstate wire communication to further the scheme.

elements.label: A scheme or artifice to defraud, or to obtain money or property by false pretenses
elements.note: A scheme is a plan. Visible posts can be part of one, and the plan itself sits behind the page.

elements.label: Use of an interstate wire communication (an online post is a communication sent by wire)
elements.note: Almost any online conduct shows this element, so it carries little weight alone.

elements.label: The communication was made to further the scheme

does_not_prove: Shown for comparison. The elements that give this definition its meaning, the scheme and the intent, sit behind the page, so the table keeps it as a comparison. Courts decide whether it applies.
